# Production candidates

Updated: 2026-11-08. US sourcing; USD. Prices retain their individual observation dates; consolidation does not refresh them.

Use this file with [Product requirements](../requirements/requirements.md) for internal hardware qualification; both can also be copied for review. This is the single human-readable list; do not create a competing candidates.txt. All durable evidence is included beside its offer in this file. Edit this Markdown directly; there is no companion candidate database or generated copy.

## Production shortlist

Approved production cameras: 0. Approved production controllers: 0.

The buy-link shortlist is the only current ranked comparison. Detailed offer
buckets below retain historical decisions, not a second recommendation list.
No exact complete configuration passes all technical, sourcing-cost, supply
and physical-acceptance requirements. No order, sample exception, deployment
or custom PCB is approved.

## Price screening

- Complete controller customer price: preferably at most $150; ceiling $250.
  Include installed >=16GB RAM, boot storage, housing, cooling and PSU.
- Adopted sourcing rule: target <=40% of intended selling price; maximum <=50%.
  At a $150 controller selling price: $60 target / $75 procurement maximum.
  At the $250 selling ceiling: $100 / $125. A $250 retail limit is not a $250
  sourcing budget. Price a separate endurance recording drive into the kit.
- Standard camera sold at $100: $40 sourcing target / $50 ceiling. Premium
  camera/doorbell sold at $150: $60 / $75. Required mounts/power, inbound
  freight and duty count. Do not relabel an ordinary camera just to fit.
- Lower intended selling prices lower these budgets. Missing charges stay
  UNKNOWN; complete assembly/testing, fulfillment/support costs and margin
  still need a costed release decision. These ratios do not guarantee profit.
- The governing limits are SRC-001 through SRC-005 in
  [production sourcing cost](../requirements/requirements.md#production-sourcing-cost).
  More expensive research samples require separate owner approval.

## Project board

- Direction: local-first Linux recorder + finished outdoor cameras; native main-stream recording/substream detection, home LAN, no recorder hotspot. Compare finished Intel appliances with off-the-shelf SoC boards plus qualified housing; no CPU label is a capacity pass.
- Current work: price-first exact Amazon/Alibaba/eBay buying links, with published facts MET, explicit failures FAIL and missing technical/commercial evidence UNKNOWN. Manufacturer pages support specifications, not an alternative shopping entry point.
- November 8: three Amazon 16GB business-PC offers refreshed below the $250 item ceiling; four camera offers refreshed below the $100 item ceiling. Complete delivered/resale economics and technical acceptance remain unqualified.
- The checked cheap eBay offers were sold, ended, unselected/out of stock or over budget. H31FX Alibaba current public price remains UNKNOWN; historical figures retain their dates.
- No exact camera, recorder or complete kit is production-approved. The earlier C500P research-only sample exception/purchase proposal remains pending, not the prerequisite for continuing documentary sourcing.
- Legacy Pi is not a production tuning target. No vendor contact, cart/order, purchase, custom PCB, Yocto migration or software port occurred. Sourcing budgets and the preferred controller price are updated; technical acceptance gates remain in force.

## Controller comparison

### Recommended controller route

Compare a finished Intel appliance with a ready-made RK3588-family single-board
computer in a qualified enclosure. A catalog board already contains the SoC,
RAM and support circuitry: this is assembly, not a custom PCB project.
The finished assembly must meet the same Linux, security, storage, thermal,
support and eight-camera requirements. No architecture is production-approved.

- Lowest integration-risk route: a finished Intel appliance, if an exact
  complete offer closes price and acceleration gates. The HP $198.99 retail
  benchmark is above the preferred $150 selling price and the $125 maximum
  production procurement budget; it is not a production sourcing fit.
- SoC route worth investigating: RK3588-family board with installed 16GB,
  reliable boot storage, PSU/cable, housing, cooling and a qualified separate
  recording-drive connection. No complete <=$150 or sourceable production
  build has been verified. Do not buy a cheap low-RAM or Lite variant instead.
- Custom carrier/SoC PCB: deferred. First compare complete catalog assemblies
  and price the integration, test and maintenance work; no board development,
  purchase or port is authorized by this research.

### Software evidence required for an RK3588 assembly

- [Frigate Rockchip decoding](https://docs.frigate.video/configuration/hardware_acceleration_video/#rockchip-platform)
  documents MPP/FFmpeg acceleration.
- [RKNN inference support](https://docs.frigate.video/configuration/object_detectors/#rockchip-platform)
  lists RK3588/RK3576, but no benchmark there qualifies our complete workload.
- [Rockchip installation](https://docs.frigate.video/frigate/installation/#rockchip-platform)
  specifies a suitable 5.10/6.1 BSP kernel, rkvdec2/rknpu drivers, RKNPU >=0.9.2
  and stable-rk container. Verify a maintained exact board/image/container
  combination; generic Ubuntu or mainline support alone does not establish it.
  Package/cache models for offline first use; a customer Internet download
  must not become mandatory. Do not ship a privileged development container.
- [Radxa hardware interface](https://docs.radxa.com/en/rock5/rock5c/hardware-design/hardware-interface)
  documents Gigabit LAN, boot-storage interfaces, power and fan connections.
  Verify endurance-drive protocol/adapter, supplied power and failure recovery.
- Required acceptance remains eight native recordings, detection across eight
  substreams, at least 30% CPU/inference headroom and 24 hours under the specified
  full load. A chip's TOPS rating or one-stream decode demo is not this result.

## Remaining research questions

These are internal remaining research questions, not a prerequisite for another outside review.

1. Qualify the refreshed HP EliteDesk 800 G4 / Lenovo M720q / Dell 3060 exact Amazon bundles: supplied PSU/rating, revision/condition, >=1GbE, maintained Linux decode AND inference, compatible separate endurance recording storage and complete delivered/resale economics. Do not confuse three refurb offers sharing a CPU class with proven capacity.
2. Resolve exact-model generic local setup, simultaneous plain H.264 main/substreams, direct local talk, reset/updates and security for the Amazon ANNKE/Anpviz camera leads. Published Windows-plugin or vendor-NVR paths are not our plug-and-play integration.
3. Complete exact-model public lifecycle/configuration/talk/update/security evidence for C500P and current FCD600. Keep each missing fact UNKNOWN; do not send suppliers questions or substitute another revision's manual.
4. Resolve the pending owner decision for a one-camera research-only sample exception and <=$100 delivered cap. No approval is implied; product requirements stay unchanged.
5. Keep Wi-Fi and wired-doorbell coverage explicitly unfilled until exact candidates meet every applicable requirement. Do not relax weather, pixel count, app-free commissioning or signed-update/identity requirements by inference.
6. After eligible hardware and acquisition approval, run the full current physical acceptance including day/night, recovery, independent media stages and eight cameras/24 hours. No synthetic or CPU-class result is a product pass.

## Board-level camera and casing research brief

### Request to the outside researcher

Determine whether OSE can meet the **unchanged attached requirements** by
assembling a readily available camera/encoder board with a compatible sensor,
optics and separately sourced enclosure, instead of buying a finished camera.
Compare purchased outdoor cases, printed cases and purchased cases with printed
internal brackets. This is a feasibility and sourcing review, not approval to
design a PCB, port firmware, buy samples or relax requirements.

The default product remains a local Linux recorder with finished cameras.
Detection belongs on the recorder: an expensive camera NPU is not a substitute
for the required video encoder, image quality, local lifecycle or complete cost.
Read the candidate buckets and their shared gaps before recommending a change.

### Routes to compare

1. **Finished camera benchmark:** use the actual exact-model offers above,
   including the C500P pack/single and other plausible PoE/Wi-Fi options. Do not
   compare a cheap bare board with a complete delivered camera, or assume a
   finished camera's closed firmware meets the security/onboarding contract.
2. **OEM/IP-camera board plus case:** a supplied sensor/ISP/encoder board, lens
   and local firmware may avoid designing a carrier PCB. Verify exact sensor
   tuning, SDK/firmware access, supported codecs/streams, audio, PoE/DC/Wi-Fi,
   updates, identity and realistic MOQ/support. Anonymous “5MP ONVIF” module
   titles are leads, not proof. A module rejected above as a finished device
   may be relevant here only as one part of a fully costed assembled camera.
3. **Supported SBC/SOM plus camera and case:** compare ready-made boards and
   carriers, not just chips. Prove the entire sensor → ISP → encoder → network
   path. Document proprietary binary/SDK dependencies and who maintains them.
   Do not assume a compatible ribbon connector or a high-MP still sensor means
   the requested encoded video modes work.

### Initial primary-source leads, not approved designs

- Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W publishes 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and H.264 encoding at 1080p30.
  Its low board price is not evidence for the required 5MP main stream or
  dual-band Wi-Fi. Do not reuse the existing legacy pilot as a product proof.
  [Official specifications](https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/raspberry-pi-zero-2-w/).
- Raspberry Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 encoder; its vendor publishes software
  encoding measurements at 1080p. This does not prove sustained 5MP main plus
  a second stream, power/thermal behavior or complete economics. It is a
  measurable software-encoding route, not an automatic encoder upgrade.
  [Vendor encoding whitepaper](https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/685-app-notes-guides-whitepapers/documents/RP-010033-WP-1-H.264%20encoding%20performance%20on%20Raspberry%20Pi%205_series%20computers.pdf).
- NXP i.MX 8M Plus advertises a high-throughput ISP and 1080p60 H.264/H.265
  encoding. The ISP's sensor resolution is not the encoder's supported frame
  geometry. Obtain an exact supported >=5MP encoding mode before calling an
  i.MX 8M Plus board plausible for this camera contract.
  [NXP industrial datasheet](https://docs.nxp.com/bundle/IMX8MPIEC/page/topics/imx_8m_plus_introduction.html).
- RV1106/RV1126 camera-oriented boards are worth checking against exact sensor,
  encoder and firmware documentation. Luckfox supplies an RV1106 datasheet and
  Core1106 boards; Boardcon documents an RV1126 module with H.264/H.265 encoding.
  Do not substitute an included 3MP sensor for a 5MP design, assume two encoded
  streams from a codec headline, or assume every “W” board has 5 GHz Wi-Fi.
  [RV1106 datasheet](https://files.luckfox.com/wiki/Luckfox-Pico/PDF/Rockchip%20RV1106%20Datasheet%20V1.3-20230522.pdf),
  [Luckfox board](https://www.luckfox.com/Core1106),
  [Boardcon module manual](https://www.boardcon.com/download/CM1126_Hardware_Manual_V1.pdf).
- Purchased enclosure families have material-specific ratings. Hammond's 1554
  page distinguishes polycarbonate outdoor-rated variants from general-purpose
  ABS variants. Verify the exact SKU, not the series name or an empty-box
  rating after adding an optical window, glands, vents, speaker and mount.

### Evidence required for each proposed assembled camera

- Exact board revision, sensor/driver/tuning, lens/mount and IR-cut arrangement;
  measured/independently documented >=5MP at >=15 FPS main plus simultaneous
  plain H.264 detection substream. State pixel dimensions, frame rates,
  bitrates, keyframes, latency and simultaneous-stream resource limits. Separate
  capture, ISP, encode and transmit limits. Decode capability is not encoding.
- Local authenticated RTSP/ONVIF, microphone, speaker and talk path; IR range,
  moving-face detail and backlit-entrance WDR. Include IR LEDs/driver, optics,
  isolation against window reflection and audio sealing, not just a bare sensor.
- Complete continuous power solution: PoE or safe PSU/DC regulation; exact
  dual-band radio/antenna path where needed. Include radio-module approvals,
  installation restrictions and assembled-device evidence; a module certificate
  or filament datasheet alone does not qualify the whole camera.
- Local first activation/network provisioning, permanent cryptographic
  identity, ownership/reset/credential rotation, signed updates/rollback and
  recovery without app/account/cloud dependence. State who controls signing
  keys, build dependencies and long-term firmware maintenance. A printed QR
  label, MAC address or filesystem serial alone is not the required identity.
- Purchased case: usable internal space, optical window, correct lens standoff,
  glands, cable strain relief, seals/gasket compression, thermal path, speaker
  membrane, mounting loads, service access, condensation and outdoor UV/temperature.
  Retest the modified assembled enclosure; do not inherit its empty-box rating.
- Printed case: exact material/process, wall orientation, print time, inserts,
  fasteners, gasket design, coating/sealing, optical window and batch variation.
  Compare UV/heat/creep, layer leakage, water jets, condensation, IR reflections,
  flammability/electrical safety, repair and reproducible assembly. “Waterproof
  filament” or a sealed prototype is not IP66 evidence. Consider printing only
  an internal bracket or sunshade inside/on a purchased rated enclosure.

### Required result

Return one short recommendation with a linked comparison and evidence gaps:

- Exact purchasable BOMs for the strongest finished, OEM-board and SBC/SOM
  routes. Include case SKU/material/drawings and sensor compatibility, current
  availability, MOQ and quantity price breaks; distinguish RFQ from orderable.
- Cost at 1, 10 and 100 units: sensor/board/lens/IR-cut/IR/audio, networking,
  power, storage/security parts, enclosure/window/glands/seals/mount, assembly,
  printing and failed prints, programming/calibration/test fixtures, yield,
  packaging, freight/duty, compliance work, warranty/spares, returns/support
  and margin. Separate one-time engineering/tooling costs from repeat cost.
  The complete standard-camera customer cap remains $100; $20-40 procurement
  is an aspiration, not a substitute hard requirement or a complete BOM price.
- A maintained-software and supply-life assessment: reproducible builds,
  camera ISP tuning, kernel/SDK updates, source/binary availability, component
  substitutions, key provisioning, vulnerability response and repairability.
- A pass/unknown/fail map to the **single requirements file**, with source URLs,
  dates and exact configurations. No implied exception for development boards,
  printed cases, 2.4-only Wi-Fi, nominal megapixels, H.265 or a lower-resolution
  substream. Quantify any requested exception separately for an owner decision.
- The smallest remaining evidence request and a costed future qualification
  plan (thermal/water/night/security/recovery and system acceptance). Do not
  start development on unknown/failing hardware or call a paper BOM approved.

If no assembled route meets the requirements and sustainable price, say so.
Identify whether the blocker is encoding/sensor software, security/lifecycle,
mechanical qualification, availability, recurring cost or one-time engineering.
Do not recommend starting a custom board simply because a cheap module exists.

Higher pixel count alone does not establish moving-person quality at night.
Sensor size, lighting, exposure and full-resolution codec behavior need actual tests.
